# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual.
My action options are limited to cutting wires 1, 2, or 3.
I need information on which wire to cut.
The Mute can read the manual and likely knows the rule (e.g., "Cut the red wire" or "If light is green, cut wire 2").
The Deaf can see the bomb's current state (colors, lights).

Since I don't know the specific configuration yet, I must rely on the others.
I will speak to the Mute first, asking for the general rule or instruction from the manual regarding wire cutting.
I will also gesture to the Deaf, asking them to indicate if there are any visible warnings or specific states I should be aware of, though without a shared language, this is risky. A better approach might be to ask the Mute to coordinate with the Deaf via me? No, Mute cannot speak. Deaf cannot hear. Only I can bridge them partially? No, I cannot see or hear/read.
Actually:
- Mute reads manual -> knows rules. Can speak to me (Blind).
- Deaf sees bomb -> knows state. Can gesture to Mute? Mute can see gestures. So Deaf can tell Mute what they see.
- Mute can then tell me what to do based on rules + observed state.

So the flow should be: Deaf signals state to Mute. Mute interprets via Manual and tells me (Blind) what to cut.

In Turn 1, I have no info. I should probably wait or ask Mute for instructions. But Mute doesn't know the state yet unless Deaf has signaled. Deaf hasn't signaled yet.
However, often in these puzzles, the initial state is static or the rule is simple.
Let's try to get the Mute to give me the *rule* first. If the rule is "Cut wire 1", I can do it. If the rule depends on color, I need that info.

I will speak to Mute asking for the defusal procedure for the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="What is the rule for cutting the wires?")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display is 0. The light is blue. The wires are Red, Yellow, and Blue from left to right. Please wait for further instructions.

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual.
My action options are limited to cutting wires 1, 2, or 3.

The Deaf monkey has sent me a message: "The display is 0. The light is blue. The wires are Red, Yellow, and Blue from left to right."
This confirms that Wire 1 is Red, Wire 2 is Yellow, and Wire 3 is Blue.
However, knowing the colors doesn't tell me *which* wire to cut unless I know the rule from the Manual.
The Mute monkey can read the Manual. The Mute monkey can hear my speech (but not gestures? No, Mute cannot speak, but can they hear? The table says Mute "Can Read the manual", "Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot hear. Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, not hear. But let's check the channels.
"When you speak, Mute receives it." -> Yes, Mute can hear me.
"When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." -> Mute can see gestures too? Or just Deaf? The prompt says "Deaf and Mute receive it". So Mute can perceive gestures.

So, I need to ask the Mute for the rule. The Mute needs to know the current state of the bomb to apply the rule.
Does the Mute know the state?
The Deaf saw the state and told *me*. Did the Deaf tell the Mute?
In Turn 1, the context was empty.
In Turn 2, I received info from Deaf.
I should relay this info to the Mute so the Mute can consult the manual and give me the instruction.

Plan:
1. Tell the Mute what the Deaf reported (Display 0, Light Blue, Wires R/Y/B).
2. Ask the Mute which wire to cut based on the manual rules for this specific configuration.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: Display is 0, Light is blue, Wires are Red(1), Yellow(2), Blue(3). What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is now orange. Mute indicates that Wire 2 (the yellow one) is the correct one to cut. Please cut Wire 2.

I am the Blind monkey. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual.
In Turn 2, I received information from Deaf about the initial state (Display 0, Light Blue, Wires R/Y/B). I relayed this to Mute and asked for instructions.
In Turn 3, Deaf reports a change: "The light is now orange." This implies the state has changed since my last observation, or perhaps the previous message was outdated/incorrect? Or maybe the light changes based on some action? I haven't acted yet.
Crucially, Deaf says: "Mute indicates that Wire 2 (the yellow one) is the correct one to cut. Please cut Wire 2."

This is a direct instruction derived from the Manual (via Mute) and the current State (via Deaf).
Deaf confirms Wire 2 is Yellow.
Mute confirms Wire 2 is the target.
I have not touched the wires yet. The prompt says "A wrong action detonates it... There is no second attempt."
However, usually in these logic puzzles, if an instruction is given clearly by the informed parties (Manual reader + Observer), it should be followed unless there's a reason to doubt it.
Is there a conflict?
Turn 2 Deaf said Light was Blue.
Turn 3 Deaf says Light is Orange.
Did something happen between turns? I didn't act. Maybe the timer ran out? Or maybe the first report was wrong? Or maybe the "Light" refers to something else?
Regardless, the *current* consensus from Deaf (who sees) and Mute (who reads rules) is to cut Wire 2.
Deaf explicitly identifies Wire 2 as the yellow one, matching my tactile knowledge of position 2 being the middle wire (assuming standard left-to-right mapping which Deaf provided earlier).

I will execute the command to cut Wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
